defects.what: The foundation-model comparison picks its baseline by substring-matching the uploaded FILENAME for 'off'/'organic', so a periodic crystal named e.g. offcut.cif is compared against MACE-OFF. That crosses two incompatible energy conventions (-1..-15 vs -100..-600 eV/atom) and the delta it prints is meaningless.

Also check an isolated molecule carrying an element outside MACE_OFF_ELEMENTS (e.g. a C10Fe cluster) returns MACE-MP-0, and that c-diamond.xyz (periodic, C only) returns MACE-MP-0.

defects.what: code.gitCommit is null in the deployed container because there is no .git in the image, so the live provenance manifest cannot pin the code that produced a result. NOMAD stamps nomad_version and nomad_commit into every public entry at build time; SimpleAtom only manages it locally.

defects.fixNote: Fixed in two places, because the runtime lookup cannot work in the image: provenance.git_info() now falls back to a GIT_COMMIT file written next to the module, and deploy-hf-space.yml writes that file from the SHA it is pushing. The same workflow was ALSO never copying provenance.py into the Space at all, so no change to that module could ever have reached production — that copy is added too (same defect class as D2). Verified by execution in a simulated Space layout with no .git and an empty PATH: gitCommit goes from null ('FileNotFoundError: ... git') to the exact pinned SHA, while dirty stays null because it cannot be checked after the fact. Two regressions checked: a real checkout still uses live git and still reports dirty=true, and an empty GIT_COMMIT still yields null with a reason rather than a fabricated SHA. NOT verified against the live hosted API — that needs a push to main, which this routine does not do.

defects.what: The force-arrow scale silently differs between models — 0.82 vs 1.0 A per eV/A on the same geometry — so two results for one molecule render non-comparable arrow lengths with no indication of the change.

It is now set by the geometry alone (1 eV/A drawn at 0.45 of the span, rung-rounded, cap 5): both models print 1.0, longest arrows 1.62 vs 2.04 A, legend tick 131.9 px for both. The screen-space tip ceiling still applies, and when it cuts the scale the legend says so — at 291x291 both models read '0.50 A per eV/A (cut from 1.0 to fit the frame)'. Measured with a Playwright script on /calculate?demo=true, Structure tab; numbers in the 5985bee commit message.
